_comment: OPENING template for the English half of the data-use demo flow. The mirror
of templates/data_use_demo_intro_es.json - read that file's comment for the
full reasoning; it is identical and is not repeated at length here.
In short: this is the one message in the flow that Meta reviews, and the
only one that is ever submitted. Consent and every ARM 2 question are sent
inside the 24-hour window that the reply to this message opens, so they need
no approval at all. Submission is irreversible - Meta has no edit operation
- so review the wording here first.
Copy matches the `intro` widget that scripts/build_data_use_demo.py emits
for English. If one changes, change the other.
Framed for UTILITY, not MARKETING. It names the session the participant is
already attending and states plainly what will happen, with no persuasion
and no incentive. Every approved opening on this account that led with
excitement or a reward landed in MARKETING, which carries per-user limits
and worse delivery. See
.claude/skills/whatsapp-template/references/ipa-examples.md.
The quick-reply button matters mechanically, not just for tone: the flow's
intro widget is send-and-wait-for-reply, so tapping Start is what opens the
24-hour window and lets every later message be free-form - including the
list pickers, which cannot open a session themselves.
'confidential' is a claim the pipeline actually keeps - encrypt_fields
encrypts name and phone before anything is stored.
This file replaces templates/rst2026_intro.json, now in templates/archive/,
which named one specific training in its body. A demo whose opener welcomes
somebody to an event they are not attending cannot be run by anyone but its
author - and the wording cannot be fixed after submission, so the event name
had to come out of the template rather than be corrected later. Spanish was
written this way from the start; English was not, and this closes the gap.
The event, the dates and the place still appear in the ARM 1 question
bodies inside the flow. Those are in-session and editable, unlike this one,
but they are equally specific - see the WARNING in build_data_use_demo.py.

twilio/quick-reply.body:
Hi {{1}}, welcome to the session on WhatsApp surveys.

During the session you will take part in a short survey - and you are also part of the example.

It takes about 3 minutes. Your answers are confidential and will only be used to illustrate WhatsApp data collection during the session.

Press Start when you are ready.
